I recently got a slightly outdated compact digital, and I've just fallen in love with some of it's results. I want to know, to up my photo game, if I'm going to have to get better equipment, or if I can get better shots by improving how I take photos.
At what point does it go from "this camera takes good pictures" to "I take good pictures?"

The thing is, an more expensive increases the chance that you take better pictures but it is not a miracle cure.

Low light conditions and conditions where you have no second chances like a wedding, it is better to have a more expensive camera.

Good photographers can take any good picture with any camera, but it comes at a cost that you need more time to take that picture and you are limited in in how much you can zoom or how close to the Sun you can point the camera to take the shot.

It is also a hidden secret that post production, Photoshop and Lightroom actually is what makes the photo more professional looking. In RAW you have more freedom than in jpg.
